transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Olivia Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Janelle Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Ben Torres (Lazuli CTO), Priya Singh (Lazuli SRE), Aaron Kim (Product), Maya Reddy (Engineering)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be rough): Discussed p95 targets and concurrency, customer worried about cost vs latency tradeoffs, interest in Dedicated for predictable latency and Private for data residency. Action: share benchmarks and schedule SE deep dive.

[00:00] Olivia Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:08] Ben Torres: Yeah hi Ben here CTO, Priya SRE, Aaron product, Maya eng. thanks for running this.
[00:15] Olivia Chen: Great. Marcus is our systems SE, he'll dig into latency and token throughput details. Marcus over to you for quick framing?
[00:24] Marcus Lee: Hey all, so we usually start by understanding expected p95 goals, average and worst case prompts, streaming needs, concurrency and whether you want hosted, dedicated or private. Also curious about your current infra.
[00:40] Priya Singh: We're running a mix - some models on-host in k8s with Triton, some smaller tasks on managed APIs. Main concern: customer-facing chat needs very low p95, around 150-200ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens) and for longer generation we can tolerate ~1s p95 but want good throughput. Also we want streaming so tokens render quickly in UI.
[01:10] Marcus Lee: okay that helps. couple clarifications - when you say p95 for short prompts is that end-to-end including network and client processing, or just inference time?
[01:22] Ben Torres: Prefer end-to-end, so from request to first token rendered in the browser. Network from our region to your hosted region is about 30-40ms typically.
[01:33] Olivia Chen: Good point. for Hosted we put customers in nearest region to minimize network hop. for Dedicated we can colocate in your cloud region and we have reserved GPU pools so latency is more predictable.
[01:47] Aaron Kim: How does streaming change the p95 number? like is the p95 measured to first token, or to completion?
[01:55] Marcus Lee: Usually p95 to first token is the metric teams care about for interactivity. streaming reduces perceived latency since first token hits sooner; we measure both first-token p95 and completion p95 during benchmarks. Also token/sec matters for throughput when you have many concurrent sessions.
[02:14] Maya Reddy: Our concurrency target is roughly 10 sustained interactive users per region for production; burst to 40 during peak. Each user could generate up to 1k tokens in a session over 30s. So token/sec and batching behavior is important.
[02:30] Marcus Lee: That's helpful - so 10 sustained with bursts to 40. we can run tests with continuous arrival patterns to measure tail latencies. quick note: depending on model size and quantization, tokens/sec varies a lot. are you evaluating a medium sized model (7-13B) or larger?
[02:46] Ben Torres: We were looking at 13B open models and also Redwood's vetted options. cost matters; if Dedicated lowers unit cost that's attractive but we need the latency guarantees.
[02:56] Priya Singh: Also security - SOC2 is a baseline, we need SAML SSO and KMS integration for keys and audit logs for every request. If private/on-prem is needed, timeline is about 3-4 months.
[03:12] Marcus Lee: we support SOC2, SAML, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs in both Dedicated and Private. Private gives you full control over keys and network. there can be additional ops lift for on-prem.
[03:25] Ben Torres: can you give rough numbers on token/sec and p95 for a 13B model on Hosted vs Dedicated?
[03:33] Marcus Lee: rough ballpark: on Hosted we run mixed workloads and for 13B you'd see first-token p95 around 250-350ms in many regions depending on network; Dedicated can push that down to ~120-180ms first-token p95 with reserved GPUs and optimized kernels, especially with batching tuned to your arrival pattern. tokens/sec for generation depends on sequence length and CPU/GPU config; for a quantized 13B on A100-ish class we might see 60-120 tokens/sec single-stream, higher in fp16 on vram heavy instances. these are ballpark, we recommend a bench with your prompt set.
[04:12] Aaron Kim: Hmm that's promising. cost delta?
[04:16] Olivia Chen: Hosted is pay-as-you-go, predictable for small scale; Dedicated has monthly commit but unit cost per token can be 30-60% lower depending on utilization. Private has licensing and ops overhead. We'll send a preliminary pricing sheet.
[04:31] Priya Singh: does KV cache or prefix caching help reduce p95 for repeating prompts? we've got lots of similar dialogs.
[04:38] Marcus Lee: yes, prefix caching and KV cache reduce repeated compute for shared prefixes and can dramatically cut end-to-end time for repeated flows. note transcription systems sometimes show KV "cash" in transcripts, ha. in practice you see huge gains for chatbots with repeat history.
[04:55] Ben Torres: what about autoscaling and burst handling for Dedicated? our traffic pattern is spiky.
[05:02] Marcus Lee: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling policies and burst pools. you can configure min reserved capacity and burst capacity that scales up with some warm-up time; critical tails can be mitigated by automatic fallbacks to slightly smaller model variants to preserve latency SLOs.
[05:18] Maya Reddy: okay on fallbacks - how seamless is model variant fallback? we worry about quality regressions.
[05:25] Olivia Chen: fallbacks are policy driven; we version and evaluate variants and you can set guardrails on quality delta. Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles and models per workload to minimize regressions. we'll share eval examples.
[05:39] Ben Torres: can you run a test with our actual prompt set and show first-token p95 and completion p95, also tokens/sec across concurrency?
[05:46] Marcus Lee: absolutely. if you can drop a sample prompt set and a representative traffic trace we'll spin up a Dedicated test node and run token/sec and p95 benchmarks.
[05:54] Ben Torres: timeline for that?
[05:57] Marcus Lee: we can get a smoke bench within a week once we have artifacts; a full run across regions and longer duration takes 2 weeks.
[06:05] Aaron Kim: what's the expected network overhead for Hosted from our EU region to your nearest region?
[06:10] Olivia Chen: usually 20-60ms depending on region pairing. EU to EU region is typically low; we'd propose hosting in eu-west to minimize network.
[06:19] Priya Singh: KMS: does Redwood support customer-managed keys in Hosted?
[06:24] Marcus Lee: yes we have customer-managed KMS options for Hosted via integrations, Dedicated gives more options, and Private you manage keys fully. there are also audit log exports.
[06:33] Ben Torres: any gotchas with streaming + batching? like does batching increase first-token latency?
[06:38] Marcus Lee: yes there's a tradeoff. batching improves throughput and unit cost but can add micro batching latency. our runtime uses continuous batching where streaming requests are prioritized to reduce first-token latency, and you can tune batching window. we'll show config tradeoffs in the bench.
[06:54] Maya Reddy: we also need to measure p95 under sustained 10 users and burst 40 users with 1k token sessions.
[06:59] Marcus Lee: noted. we'll run sustained and burst profiles, measure first-token p95, completion p95, and tokens/sec. also track GPU utilization and egress.
[07:10] Aaron Kim: any limits on concurrent streaming connections?
[07:14] Olivia Chen: Hosted has soft limits and quotas, Dedicated you can configure higher concurrency, and Private depends on your infra. for 40 concurrent streaming chats with 1k tokens each, Dedicated is likely the right fit for cost predictability.
[07:28] Ben Torres: competitor question - we also looked at Anthropic and OpenAI - how does Redwood compare on latency?
[07:34] Marcus Lee: we position to be competitive; some managed providers have great latency in specific regions but our strength is predictable Dedicated latency and deployment flexibility (private, VPC). plus observability tools to debug token-level latency.
[07:47] Priya Singh: last thing - data residency. can we ensure logs and telemetry stay in region?
[07:53] Olivia Chen: yes Dedicated and Private can be constrained to region; Hosted also offers regional tenancy in many regions. we'll include data residency docs.
[08:02] Ben Torres: ok great. next steps summary?
[08:05] Olivia Chen: we'll: 1) share benchmark spreadsheet and preliminary pricing, 2) Marcus will run smoke test once you share prompt set, 3) schedule SE deep dive next Tue (3/10) - Marcus can you lead?
[08:18] Marcus Lee: yes I'll lead the deep dive and bench.
[08:21] Aaron Kim: we aim to decide by end of month after bench results.
[08:25] Olivia Chen: perfect. thanks everyone.

(occasional crosstalk and filler):
[08:30] Priya Singh: mm hm, yep, okay thanks, bye
[08:33] Maya Reddy: thanks

End of transcript.
